newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to complete loan payment in December.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to complete loan payment in December.

text.p: Kuwait will complete paying off a $5.5 billion sovereign loan and outstanding principle on schedule in December, bankers said on Sunday.
They said Kuwait, which like other oil exporters is enjoying added revenue from higher world oil prices, had made one payment of about $785 million in September with the final one due in December.
Kuwait's Central Bank Governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al- Sabah was quoted on Sunday by local dailies as saying the final payment of $800 million would be made in December.
"With the final payment Kuwait will have no outstanding long-term foreign debts," one banker said.
Sheikh Salem was quoted last year as saying his country would not borrow from international markets again.
Kuwait took the jumbo loan, arranged by J.P. Morgan and Co, following Iraq's 1990-91 occupation of the tiny state.
At the time it was the largest ever made to a sovereign state. The main lending banks were from Japan, France, Germany the United States and some Arab countries.
Bankers also reported on Sunday a 1.196 billion dinars ($4 billion) surplus in Kuwait's 1995 government investment account compared to a deficit of one billion dinars the previous year.

Kuwait's 4.21 billion dinar budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July- June) carries a forecast net deficit of 1.21 billion dinars but oil revenue was calculated at a weighted average barrel price of $13 while current world prices are well over $20 a barrel.
Kuwait produces about two million barrels of oil a day.
